Here are the artificial penalty/slack variables in `equations.gms` files used to prevent infeasibility across the optimization:

| Location | Slack variable | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `core/equations.gms:947` | `v_changeProdStartyearSlack` | Loosens the startyear production-change equation so the model can always "allow some change" (bounded by `.up`/`.lo` on the slack) instead of hitting an infeasible fixed reference. |
| `modules/21_tax/on/equations.gms:356` | `v21_emiAllco2neg_slack` | Positive slack absorbing the gap between `vm_emiAll` and its negative-emissions counterpart so the identity always balances instead of forcing infeasibility when emissions are positive. |
| `modules/21_tax/on/equations.gms:365` | `v21_emiAllco2neg_acrossIterations_slack` | Same pattern across-iterations: absorbs the gap between CDR and the prior-iteration reference gross emissions. |
| `modules/31_fossil/timeDepGrades/equations.gms` (142–168) and `modules/31_fossil/MOFEX/equations.gms` (89–115) | `v31_fuSlack` | Absorbs leftover extraction capacity from early-retired oil wells so the resource-depletion equation doesn't become infeasible. |
| `modules/36_buildings/simple/equations.gms:43,63` | `v36_expSlack` | Slack on the logistic H2-cost-exponent equation (with a tiny `1e-8` cost penalty in the cost equation) to keep the barrier-cost formulation feasible at extreme penetration levels. |

Common pattern: each slack is a positive variable added/subtracted in an `=e=` identity so the equation can always balance; a small or implicit cost (e.g. the `1e-8` weight in `q36_costAddH2PhaseIn`) discourages the optimizer from using the slack unless truly needed, similar to a soft-constraint penalty.

Note `v_changeProdStartyearSlack`, `v21_emiAllco2neg_slack`, `v21_emiAllco2neg_acrossIterations_slack`, `v31_fuSlack`, and `v36_expSlack` are the actual GAMS variable names — I did not check their `.up`/`.lo` bound declarations, so if you want the exact tightness of each slack (bounds file), I can look those up next.
